items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: Start off listening to Lester Young.

ctx.x: I thought of this question when you said your wife was a singer. Do you play a melody of a tune differently if it has a well-known lyric?

You know ever since I’ve been married, yes. I mean now I know a lot of the words, I’m not going to lie to you and say I studied the words, even though Lester Young did and a lot of people do. But I’m playing with my wife a lot more, you know, and I hear the lyrics. You know I’m on the bandstand and I listen to her sing, and I say wow that’s a great lyric. And she’s great, and she writes lyrics. And we just did a gig at Cornelia Street in the Village, it was totally jammed. And the reason why they hired her, and…
What’s it like to, is your wife professional? I mean does she make her living singing?
